newsitem.title: BULGARIA: EU TO LEND BULGARIA 250 MLN ECU FOR BUDGET SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: EU TO LEND BULGARIA 250 MLN ECU FOR BUDGET SUPPORT.

text.p: The European Commission is close to finalising a 250 million Ecu ($278 million) macrofinancial loan facility for Bulgaria and expects to release the first instalment this autumn, the commission said on Thursday.

A commission statement praised Bulgaria's "courageous" reform programme and said the commission would support elaboration of a new pre-accession partnership to prepare Bulgaria for eventual European Union membership.

"Bulgaria expects to receive this autumn the first tranche amounting to 120 million Ecu from the European Union's financial support for the country's balance of payments," Finance Minister Muravei Radev told Reuters.

European Union support for Bulgaria in 1997 includes a EURATOM loan of up to 150 million Ecu to ensure a safe and reliable electricity supply, grant support of up to 40 million Ecu from the PHARE programme for structural adjustment and strengthening of the social safety net, and PHARE cash handouts to the poorest Bulgarians of 20 million Ecu early this year.

The statement said the Commission expressed "satisfaction with the considerable progress made by Bulgaria in recent months and with the evident commitment of the Bulgarian authorities to far-reaching and irreversible structural reforms".

The interim government appointed in February and their elected successors who took office in May have stabilised the economy, stepped up privatisations and begun liquidating or selling loss-making state enterprises.
On July 1, the government introduced a currency board system, fixing the lev at 1,000 to the mark to stabilise the currency and lower inflation.
